idiom_name: plain objects + model/schema defined outside the entity (Sequelize, Mongoose)
implementation_notes: JavaScript entities are already persistence-ignorant: instances are plain objects and there is no entity class structure to strip. The metadata lives in a model definition created outside the entity - sequelize.define(name, attributes, options) or Model.init(attributes) for SQL, new Schema({...}) for MongoDB - and the model class or model object is the persistence facade (findAll/save). That schema object replaces the classic per-class mapping code; a hand-written mapping function is the simpler replacement when a single table needs no ORM. Attributes carry field, type and constraint metadata, so the entity itself stays a plain object.
pitfalls: Mapper instances are not plain data: Sequelize/Mongoose add getters, setters and internal state, so naive spread/JSON serialization can lose or leak fields.
The model API (save/destroy) turns the class into an Active Record; keep those calls behind a repository/service boundary if the separation is to survive.
Schema metadata and business objects drift independently - adding an attribute adds no behaviour and nothing checks the domain expectations against it.
